gi17_un.topic: UN Security Council and General Assembly since Oct 2023

claims.text: UNSC Resolution 2803 adopted 17 Nov 2025 by 13-0 with China and Russia abstaining; endorsed the October 2025 Gaza plan, welcomed a Board of Peace, authorized an International Stabilization Force; Netanyahu welcomed it; the PA welcomed it; Hamas denounced it; Russia said it gives 'complete control over the Gaza strip to the Board of Peace'.

In June 2025 the US vetoed a Security Council draft demanding an immediate, unconditional and permanent Gaza ceasefire and unrestricted aid, backed by the other 14 members; the US cited Hamas's 'failure to disarm' and said the draft did not address Israel's security or hostage release.

UN General Assembly, June 2025: resolution demanding an 'immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire', release of hostages and resumed aid adopted 149-12 (Israel and US against) with 19 abstentions.

12 Sep 2025: the General Assembly endorsed the France-Saudi 'New York Declaration' 142-10-12 (Israel and US against); it condemns Hamas's 7 October attacks, demands Hamas free all hostages, end its rule in Gaza and hand weapons to the PA.

Israel's foreign ministry spokesman Oren Marmorstein said Israel 'utterly rejects' the declaration, called the Assembly 'a political circus detached from reality' and said it 'encourages Hamas to continue the war'.

claims.text: ICJ order of 28 March 2024, citing 'the spread of famine and starvation': reaffirmed the January measures 14-2 (Sebutinde, Barak against); unanimously ordered Israel to ensure 'unhindered provision at scale' of food, water, electricity, fuel, shelter and medical care, including more land crossings; 15-1 that its military not commit acts violating Palestinians' Genocide Convention rights including by preventing aid; report within one month.

UK: Foreign Secretary Lammy suspended about 30 of 350 export licences in Sept 2024; the suspension did not cover F-35 parts. On 30 June 2025 the High Court (Males, Steyn) rejected Al-Haq's challenge, calling the issue 'a matter for the executive'; Defence Secretary Healey said suspension would affect the 'whole F-35 programme'.

Netherlands: Feb 2024 appeals court ordered a halt to F-35 parts exports; on 3 Oct 2025 the Supreme Court held the appeals court could not make its own risk assessment and ordered the minister to reassess within six weeks, the halt remaining meanwhile; the government had argued foreign policy is for government and the US would supply the parts anyway.
On 14 Nov 2025 the Dutch cabinet said it would keep halting F-35 parts shipments to Israel pending a final decision within six months; since April 2025 export permits to Israel assessed case by case.

gi17_states.topic: States: recognitions, arms, sanctions, trade, Arab and Turkish positions

claims.text: 22 May 2024: Ireland, Spain and Norway announced recognition of a Palestinian state (Norway's effective 28 May, on pre-4 June 1967 lines); Israel recalled its envoys to Ireland and Norway; Israel's foreign minister said Israel 'will not back down against those who undermine its sovereignty'; Ireland cited 'appalling' conditions in Gaza; Norway the Palestinians' 'fundamental, independent right to self-determination'.

Sept 2025: the UK (21 Sept), Canada, Australia, Portugal, France, Belgium, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco and Andorra recognised Palestine; 157 of 193 UN members recognise it; 11 new recognitions in 2025 and 20 since Oct 2023 (per Al Jazeera); Netanyahu called UK recognition a 'prize' for Hamas and said a Palestinian state 'will not happen'; Danon called the summit a 'circus'.

Germany: Merz restricted exports of arms that could be used in Gaza in Aug 2025 after the Israeli cabinet's Gaza City decision; lifted from 24 Nov 2025, spokesman Hille citing the 10 Oct ceasefire; SIPRI: Germany supplied 30% of Israel's major arms imports 2019-23; Saar urged others to follow Germany; Israel had said in August such moves 'reward terrorism'.

10 Jun 2025: Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Norway and the UK imposed asset freezes and travel bans on Ben-Gvir and Smotrich, saying they 'have incited extremist violence and serious abuses of Palestinian human rights'; Saar called it 'outrageous'; US State Department spokesperson Tammy Bruce called it 'extremely unhelpful'; Smotrich expressed 'contempt'.

EU, April 2026: the Commission's Sept 2025 proposal to suspend trade provisions of the Association Agreement (about EUR 5.8bn of Israeli exports) lacked a qualified majority; Spain, Ireland, Belgium in favour; Germany, Denmark, Netherlands reluctant; Israel had called the proposal 'morally and politically distorted'.

11 May 2026: EU foreign ministers unanimously agreed in principle to sanction Hamas leaders and Israeli settler figures after Orban's April election defeat ended Hungary's veto; Haaretz reported the draft list includes Amana, Nachala, Hashomer Yosh, Regavim, Daniella Weiss; no ministers reported; trade suspension not agreed; Kallas: 'high time we move from deadlock to delivery'; Saar: 'arbitrary and political'.

Turkey announced in May 2024 it would stop all trade with Israel until aid flowed into Gaza; on 29 Aug 2025 FM Hakan Fidan said Turkey had severed all economic and commercial ties, barred its ships from Israeli ports and announced an airspace ban (scope unclear; flight trackers showed Israeli flights still crossing); 2023 bilateral trade nearly $6.8bn.

Kazakhstan, with relations with Israel since 1992, announced on 6 Nov 2025 it would join the Abraham Accords; the UAE and other Accords states have maintained trade and security ties with Israel; Saudi officials stress the Arab Peace Initiative.
